summary.limits: Ready means only that one explicit call exactly equals one member of a complete matching historical rehearsal set within the reviewer-declared age window. It is not approval, authorization, a signature, or permission to send. The caller may be a contract and need not be an available transaction origin. No current state, future inclusion, gas, fees, nonce, effects, ABI authenticity, authority, wallet, provider identity, or chain authenticity is established. Calls in the set are independent; no writes are simulated. Nothing is sent.

Fresh means only complete matching historical provider evidence inside the reviewer-declared age window. The review time is an input, not an independently verified clock. The window is a review policy, not a guarantee against state changes. No current state, future execution, gas, authority, ABI authenticity, provider identity or chain authenticity is established. Calls are independent and do not share simulated writes. No network request or transaction is made.

Bound means complete matching historical provider evidence for independent calls at one exact block. Calls do not share simulated writes: this is not a sequence, multicall, atomic transaction, or state-effect simulation. Order has no execution meaning. Expected bytes are supplied by the reviewer; an expected ABI false can match. No ABI authentication, gas, fees, nonce, authority, current state or future success is established. Digests identify content, not authenticity. Nothing is sent.

Independent historical calls, not a stateful sequence or multicall. Signatures and return layouts are reviewer choices, not authenticated ABI. Selector patterns do not establish reachability or behavior. Code inclusion is relative to supplied headers; call returns remain unproven RPC claims. An anchor hash is an equality check, not authentication. No current-state, authority, gas, effects, safety, or future-execution guarantee. Nothing is sent.

Bound means only that this explicit call and expected bytes match saved provider evidence at the exact reviewed historical block. It is not approval to transact. The sender may be a contract: this does not prove that anyone can originate the call. No nonce, gas, fees, access list, wallet wrapping, signatures, state effects, ABI meaning, balances, current state or future success are checked. Even a returned ABI false may be bound if those exact bytes were expected. Digests identify input content; they do not authenticate a provider or the chain. Nothing is sent.

The signature and return layout are reviewer choices, not an authenticated ABI. A selector collision or unreachable pattern can match. Code inclusion is relative to the supplied header; its authenticity is not established by this tool. Call arguments and returns are historical RPC claims, not locally executed or proved state effects. No freshness, balance availability for spending, permissions, gas, routing, safety or future execution is established. Nothing is signed or sent.

Argument types are supplied by the reviewer and are not inferred from the selector. A decoded calldata payload does not authenticate an ABI, establish intended effects, permissions, balances, gas, safety, current state, or future execution. It makes no network request and does not sign, send, pay, post, or deploy anything.

Aligned historical evidence is not a verified ABI, routing or reachability proof, code approval, current-state check, permission to transact or execution guarantee. Return types and signature are caller choices. The code proof is unanchored unless the caller independently supplies an authentic block hash; call returns remain unproven RPC claims even when code inclusion verifies. Nothing is signed or sent.

Types are supplied by the reviewer, not inferred or authenticated. Decoding does not establish the contract ABI, expected outcome, safety, state changes, gas, canonicality or future execution. Historical provider claims only. No transaction is signed or sent.

An untrusted, historical RPC rehearsal is only compared with a declared Unix time. A current verdict does not prove a transaction is safe, executable, canonical, included, or unchanged now. It does not obtain a clock or make a network request. Nothing is signed, sent, paid, or deployed.

Provider-reported simulation at a finalized historical state; no transaction sent. No gas estimate, receipt, state diff, authenticity proof or guarantee of future execution. Contributor relay used; source is public attribution only. Upstream provider identity and independence are not verified.

Checks unauthenticated historical provider claims, not EVM execution proofs. A reported revert may be misclassified by an RPC. A match proves no access control, state effects, safety, canonicality, provider independence or future refusal. reported_revert requires no bytes and makes no claim about the reason. Nothing sent.

Checks saved provider claims against a declared expectation at one historical block. A match is not transaction success, token movement, gas estimation, authentication, provider independence or a guarantee of future execution. Nothing sent.
